item.title: A quick squeeze helps CRISPR turn skin cells into neurons more efficiently
item.description: Human cells hold about two meters (6.6 feet) of DNA, folded and compacted to fit inside a nucleus. That packing is essential for life, but it creates a problem for scientists. item.title: East Asia's summer rain belt has shifted north over decades, reshaping rain and heat risks
item.description: A joint research team from KAIST and the APEC Climate Center has found that the East Asian summer front has migrated north over the past half century, with the shift exceeding 200 km (124 miles) in late summer. This raises the risk that the Korean Peninsula will experience heavy rain and heat stress at the same time. The findings suggest that summer disaster planning should address flood prevention and heat-illness management together, through late September. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Albert Einstein's 100-year-old handwritten letter filled with equations sells for $71,811
item.description: A handwritten letter by Albert Einstein, believed to date back to around 1929, has sold for $71,811 at RR Auction. Addressed to mathematician Chaim Herman Muntz, the one-page document contains detailed equations exploring Hamiltonian mechanics, covariance and invariance. Written in German, the letter was sold with its original envelope, postmarked in Potsdam, offering a glimpse into Einstein's mathematical discussions nearly a century ago.
